title: Pairs Trading: Performance of a Relative-Value Arbitrage Rule
research_question: Does the Wall Street pairs rule earn excess returns?
mechanism: Temporary mispricing of close substitutes; common factor in returns
methodology: Distance method: min SSD of normalized prices over formation, trade 2-sigma divergences; bootstrap vs reversal
out_of_sample: Not stated in abstract (formation then trading period in method, from memory; unverified)
main_findings: Annualized excess returns up to 11% for self-financing pair portfolios; profits typically exceed conservative cost estimates; effect differs from known reversal profits
limitations: Sample ends 2002; later work (L02,L03,L05) finds decay
replicable_with_free_data: Partial (CRSP paid; ETF/stock proxies free but different)
retail_feasibility: Low-medium: equity shorting/borrow costs, daily rebalancing; original sample not current

title: Does Simple Pairs Trading Still Work?
research_question: Has pairs trading profitability decayed?
period: through ~GFC (exact start not seen in abstract)
methodology: Replication/extension of GGR distance method with alternative algorithms
costs_included: See L03 for explicit costs; abstract silent
main_findings: Confirms continuing downward trend in profitability; strong in prolonged turbulence incl. GFC; alternative algorithms plus other measures add 22 bps/month for bank stocks
limitations: Abstract only seen; costs treatment not in abstract

title: Are Pairs Trading Profits Robust to Trading Costs?
research_question: Do pairs profits survive commissions, market impact, short fees?
methodology: Distance pairs within refined industry groups; compare to short-term reversal
costs_included: Yes: commissions, market impact, short selling fees
main_findings: Still profitable but 'much more modest': ~30 bps/month risk-adjusted among well-matched industry pairs; SSRN version: top-30% largest stocks alpha 24 bps/month; both contrarian types largely unprofitable after 2002
retail_feasibility: Low: net edge ~30 bps/month before retail frictions

title: Statistical Arbitrage Pairs Trading Strategies: Review and Outlook
research_question: What do >100 pairs trading references show, by approach?
mechanism: Taxonomy: distance, cointegration, time-series, stochastic control, other
methodology: Literature survey; reviews profitability under market frictions
main_findings: Five-category taxonomy; profitability reviewed in light of market frictions; strengths and weaknesses of each approach assessed
limitations: Survey; no new data; abstract gives no profitability numbers

title: The Profitability of Pairs Trading Strategies: Distance, Cointegration and Copula Methods
research_question: Which pairs method is best net of costs, and does it persist?
methodology: Distance, cointegration, copula (2-step) with time-varying trading costs; factor alphas
main_findings: Mean monthly excess return 91/85/43 bps before costs and 38/33/5 bps after costs (distance/cointegration/copula); from 2009 trading opportunities via distance and cointegration fall considerably; all alphas positive after risk factors

title: Statistical Arbitrage in the US Equities Market
research_question: Do PCA/ETF residual mean-reversion strategies earn alpha?
mechanism: Mean-reverting idiosyncratic residuals vs PCA factors or sector ETFs
methodology: PCA and ETF factor residuals, OU s-score, market neutral
costs_included: Costs per search summary of working draft (not verified in paper)
main_findings: Via web-search summaries of the abstract (not opened directly): ETF strategies Sharpe 1.1 over 1997-2007 with degradation since 2002; PCA strategies average Sharpe 0.9 in 2003-2007; volume-adjusted ETF 1.51 in 2003-2007. Working draft cites 1.44 after costs 1997-2007 for PCA (unverified)
limitations: Figures seen only via search-result summaries; pre-2008 sample; needs many-stock universe
retail_feasibility: Low: needs broad short-capable universe and low costs

title: Empirical Investigation of an Equity Pairs Trading Strategy
research_question: What drives pairs trading profits?
mechanism: Short-term reversal plus pairs momentum (industry momentum)
methodology: Return-based pairs signal decomposed; factor regressions
main_findings: Large significant abnormal returns; profits largely explained by short-term reversal and one-month industry momentum
limitations: Little claim of a distinct arbitrage; abstract-level read

title: An Anatomy of Pairs Trading: The Role of Idiosyncratic News, Common Information and Liquidity
research_question: Where do pairs profits come from?
mechanism: Liquidity provision/price discovery: profits higher after liquidity-driven or lead-lag news divergence
methodology: Conditioning pair divergences on news types
main_findings: Profits are higher when divergence stems from news that temporarily reduces liquidity of one stock or affects both with one reacting faster

title: From Cointegration to Out-of-Sample Failure: A Pairs-Trading Case Study on PEP-KO
research_question: Is a cointegration pairs strategy robust OOS?
methodology: Cointegration, in-sample threshold optimisation, cost/parameter sensitivity, walk-forward, Adjusted & Deflated Sharpe, rolling OLS/Kalman
main_findings: Weakening mean-reversion dynamics undermine strategy OOS
limitations: Single pair preprint, not peer reviewed; no numbers quoted

title: Crypto Carry
research_question: What drives crypto futures-spot carry and is it arbitrageable?
mechanism: Convenience yield from leverage-seeking trend-chasing retail demand; limited arbitrage capital (margin/regulatory frictions)
main_findings: Carry can exceed 40% p.a. (MS abstract; BIS 2023 version: up to 60%); search summary of BIS paper: average about 7% p.a.; arbitrage risky due to margin spikes and liquidations in drawdowns; high carry predicts crashes (per summary)
limitations: Average-level figure seen only via search summary; institutional focus
retail_feasibility: Medium: cash-and-carry doable but margin/liquidation and exchange risk

title: Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures
research_question: How should perpetual futures be priced and are deviations exploitable?
mechanism: Funding rate anchors perp to spot; no-arbitrage price and bounds with trading costs
methodology: No-arbitrage pricing; empirical deviations; implied arbitrage strategy
main_findings: Deviations in crypto larger than in traditional currency markets, comove across currencies, diminish over time; implied arbitrage strategy yields high Sharpe ratios (no figure in abstract)
limitations: Sharpe magnitudes not seen; published venue not verified

title: The Crypto Carry Trade
research_question: Is short perp/futures + long spot profitable?
instruments: Derivative contracts on one of the largest crypto exchanges (abstract)
main_findings: In-sample annual Sharpe 7 to 10 ('unusually profitable'); insights on exchange-specific risks
limitations: In-sample, 2022 draft, exchange counterparty risks; later periods likely compressed

title: Perpetual Futures Pricing
research_question: No-arbitrage price of perpetual contracts
mechanism: Periodic funding anchors futures to spot
main_findings: Futures price = risk-neutral expectation of spot sampled at a random time; funding specifications guaranteeing no-arbitrage identified

title: Trading and Arbitrage in Cryptocurrency Markets
research_question: Are crypto prices consistent across exchanges?
mechanism: Capital controls and segmented markets limit arbitrage
methodology: Cross-exchange price gap analysis; order flow decomposition
main_findings: Per web-search summary: large recurrent arbitrage deviations persisting for weeks; gaps much larger across than within countries; common order flow component about 80% of bitcoin returns (published)
limitations: Abstract not directly opened; early period before market maturation (see L15)

title: Arbitrage in the Market for Cryptocurrencies
research_question: Do cross-exchange arbitrage opportunities remain exploitable?
main_findings: Opportunities exist but magnitude decreased greatly from April 2018; barely possible to exploit since then; informed trading correlates with fewer opportunities

title: Building Trust Takes Time: Limits to Arbitrage for Blockchain-Based Assets
research_question: Why do cross-exchange gaps persist?
mechanism: Settlement latency creates price risk; off-chain settlement creates default risk
methodology: Empirical on latency and price gaps
main_findings: Price differences coincide with high settlement latency; flows chase arbitrage; smaller gaps among low-default-risk exchanges

title: Pairs Trading in Cryptocurrency Markets
research_question: Do distance/cointegration pairs work in crypto?
costs_included: Sensitivity to transaction costs/execution windows reported
main_findings: Strategies underperform classical benchmarks; daily distance method -0.07%/month vs 11.61%/month at 5-minute frequency; sensitive to parameters and costs

title: Constructing Cointegrated Cryptocurrency Portfolios for Statistical Arbitrage
research_question: Can cointegrated crypto baskets be traded?
main_findings: Cointegrated portfolios of four cryptos found; trading systems with stop-losses tested (results not in abstract excerpt)

title: Copula-Based Trading of Cointegrated Cryptocurrency Pairs
research_question: Does a copula improve crypto pairs trading?
main_findings: Authors report method outperforms prior cointegration/copula pair strategies in profitability and risk-adjusted returns

title: The Relationship Between Arbitrage in Futures and Spot Markets and Bitcoin Price Movements
research_question: Do Bitcoin futures-spot arbitrage opportunities exist?
main_findings: Few arbitrage opportunities in normal markets; large ones arise in crashes

title: Carry
research_question: Does carry predict returns across assets?
instruments: Equities, bonds, commodities, Treasuries, credit, options, FX
main_findings: Carry predicts returns cross-sectionally and in time series; not explained by known predictors and captures many; carry underperforms in recessions/liquidity/vol episodes (per search summary)
limitations: Implementation via liquid futures; costs not in abstract

title: The Fundamentals of Commodity Futures Returns
research_question: What drives commodity futures risk premia?
mechanism: Inventories drive convenience yield; basis, momentum are state signals
methodology: Inventory-based analysis of basis and momentum
main_findings: Risk premia vary across commodities and over time with inventory levels; futures basis, past returns informative

authors: Szymanowska, de Roon, Nijman, van den Goorbergh
title: An Anatomy of Commodity Futures Risk Premia
research_question: Spot vs term premia in commodity futures
mechanism: Spot premia and term premia (basis changes)
methodology: Sorts on basis, momentum, vol, inflation, hedging pressure, liquidity
main_findings: Spot premia between 5% and 14% per annum and term premia between 1% and 3% (abstract)
limitations: Before costs per abstract; not retail-implementable as is

title: Value and Momentum Everywhere
research_question: Do value and momentum exist in all asset classes?
instruments: 8 markets/asset classes incl. currencies and commodities
main_findings: Consistent value and momentum premia in every asset class; value and momentum negatively correlated

title: Momentum Strategies in Commodity Futures Markets
venue: SSRN working paper 702281 (2005); published Journal of Banking & Finance (not verified)
research_question: Do commodity futures show momentum/reversal?
main_findings: Contrarian does not work; 13 profitable momentum strategies earn 9.38% average per year; they buy backwardated and sell contangoed

title: Soybean Crush Spread Arbitrage: Trading Strategies and Market Efficiency
research_question: Revisits Simon (1999) crush spread arbitrage
main_findings: Contrary to Simon, winning trades are significantly shorter than losing trades; suggests rules to avoid lengthy trades

title: ... and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns
research_question: What significance hurdle after massive data mining?
methodology: Multiple testing adjustments with correlation and publication bias
main_findings: New factor needs t-statistic greater than 3.0; most claimed findings in financial economics likely false

title: False (and Missed) Discoveries in Financial Economics
research_question: Calibrate Type I and II error in factor/fund selection
methodology: Double-bootstrap t-hurdles for a target FDR, ratio of misses to false discoveries
main_findings: Establishes t hurdle for a given false discovery rate; current methods lack power (abstract truncated in my view)

title: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting and Non-Normality
venue: SSRN 2460551 (also Journal of Portfolio Management; not verified here)
research_question: How to deflate Sharpe for number of trials/non-normality?
methodology: DSR adjusting for trials and skew/kurtosis
main_findings: DSR corrects for selection bias under multiple testing and non-normal returns, separating findings from flukes

authors: Bailey, Borwein, Lopez de Prado, Zhu
title: The Probability of Backtest Overfitting
research_question: Probability that selected backtest is overfit
main_findings: Hold-out tends to be unreliable for investment backtests; CSCV gives accurate PBO estimates
limitations: Needs the full matrix of tried configurations

title: A Reality Check for Data Snooping
research_question: Test best rule among many vs benchmark
main_findings: Provides data-snooping adjusted test (abstract not opened by me)

title: A Test for Superior Predictive Ability
research_question: More powerful alternative to Reality Check
main_findings: More powerful and less sensitive to poor and irrelevant alternatives than White RC (Monte Carlo)

title: Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability?
research_question: How much do published anomalies decay?
main_findings: Returns 26% lower OOS and 58% lower post-publication; 32% attributable to publication-informed trading; higher in-sample returns decay more

title: Replicating Anomalies
research_question: Do anomalies survive standard testing?
main_findings: 65% of 452 anomalies fail |t|>1.96; 96% of trading-friction category; higher hurdle 2.78 cited

title: The Adaptive Markets Hypothesis: Evidence from the Foreign Exchange Market
venue: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 44(2):467-488
research_question: Do published FX trading rule profits persist OOS?
methodology: True OOS tests of published rules
main_findings: 1970s-80s excess returns genuine, not data mining, but disappeared by early 1990s for filter and MA rules

title: Common Risk Factors in Currency Markets
research_question: Do carry portfolios earn a premium?
main_findings: Spread between lowest and highest interest-rate currency portfolios exceeds 5 percentage points p.a. 1983-2007 after bid-ask spreads
limitations: Abstract truncated in my view; carry crash risk

title: Currency Momentum Strategies
venue: SSRN working paper 1971680 (published JFE; not verified)
research_question: Does momentum exist in FX?
main_findings: Cross-sectional spread up to 10% p.a. between winner and loser currencies, not explained by traditional risk factors, partially explained by transaction costs
